units.function: Four newline-delimited JSON-RPC worker fixtures for delayed execution, streamed-log forgery/oversize, nested host-request invocation scope and classified termination.
units.dependencyDirection: Standalone Node child-process fixtures -> stdin/stdout JSON-RPC -> host plugin-worker-manager tests; they do not import Paperclip packages, access network/files/database, call models or represent production Agents.
units.keyDataModels: JSON-RPC request/result/error/notification, worker supported methods, invocation envelope/ID, execute.log stream/chunk, nested company/Secret/state/event request and termination code.
units.lifecycle: Initialize worker -> receive host invocation -> optionally delay, emit valid/forged/oversized logs or issue a nested host request with own/missing/unknown scope -> return result/error -> acknowledge shutdown and exit.
units.testAssessment: All four CommonJS fixtures passed node --check. They are exercised behaviorally by the later plugin-worker-manager unit, which was intentionally not pre-read; these files themselves have no assertions and omit malformed-JSON resilience, cancel, crash/restart and backpressure fixtures.
units.designRationale: Use tiny deterministic adversarial processes to test the real child-process framing and host trust boundary, including a single reused worker that remembers another invocation and attempts cross-company log or nested-call forgery.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a public Connector/Plugin conformance and adversarial suite proving that a multi-tenant worker cannot forge company, Work, invocation, logs, Secret or event scope and that timeout/termination behavior is deterministic without real credentials.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT these as seeds for Connector SDK adversarial fixtures. Use vendor-neutral names and typed protocol versions; add malformed framing, cancellation acknowledgment, crash/signal, partial side effects, idempotent retry, stdout/stderr backpressure, capability/version mismatch, approval pause/resume, evidence digest and secret-free attestation cases.
units.responsibilityConflict: Invocation scoping is necessary but contains no accountable human, ResponsibilityContract, DataAuthorization or Approval binding. The fixtures test host isolation only and must not be presented as real Agent behavior or responsibility evidence.
units.securityFindings: POSITIVE adversarial coverage: prior invocation log forgery and method-specific nested company scope are modeled explicitly. HIGH missing protocol cases: malformed/oversized result framing, cancellation, crash/signal, restart and backpressure are absent. HIGH responsibility gap: invocation ID alone is not a Work/contract/approval/data grant. MEDIUM error-contract gap: termination uses numeric -32002 plus a display message rather than a demonstrated stable typed cause.
